items.claim: Provider dispatch table is unreachable by credential-free tests
items.consequence: If an environment variable is ever paired with the wrong backup function in the new table, the affected provider's repositories silently stop being backed up (or the run fails with another provider's "token is not set" error), and the test run that gates this PR stays green. collectProviderBackupResults is reached only through Run(), and every test that gets Run() past validation is a live test that skips without provider credentials (15 skips in the recorded run). Swapping the GitHub and Gitlab entries on a scratch copy of the reviewed commit left all credential-free tests passing. The repo already has a hermetic GitHub mock (newGitFixtureServer/newGitHubMockAPI), and GitHub() reads GITHUB_APIURL, so one Run()-level test can cover the table, validateStartupConfig, createWorkingDir and the one-shot path of scheduleBackups without credentials.
items.proposedFix: Add a hermetic test in internal/github_mock_test.go that reuses newGitFixtureServer and newGitHubMockAPI, then sets (t.Setenv) GIT_BACKUP_DIR=t.TempDir(), GITHUB_TOKEN=mock-token, GITHUB_APIURL=api.URL, GITHUB_BACKUPS=1, unsets every other provider variable and GIT_BACKUP_INTERVAL/GIT_BACKUP_CRON, calls resetGlobals() and require.NoError(t, Run()), and asserts the same bundle files TestGithubRepositoryBackupWithMockAPI asserts under <backupDir>/github.com/mockuser/<repo>. Assumption: the mock serves everything GitHub() requests when driven through the package httpClient; note execProviderBackups calls os.Exit(1) on a failed provider, so a failure aborts the test binary rather than reporting a normal assertion. If that is unacceptable, alternatively extract the env-var selection into a function returning the selected provider names and assert it per env var.
items.notes: Every original item, known problem and corrective request was assessed.

claims.quote: Provider dispatch table is unreachable by credential-free tests
claims.notes: The comment says no test reaches the new tokenProviders table in collectProviderBackupResults unless provider credentials are present, so a wrong env-var/provider pairing would pass the suite. That is true from the source. collectProviderBackupResults is called only from runProviderBackups, which is reached only through Run -> scheduleBackups -> execProviderBackups. The two credential-free tests that call Run fail before that point: TestGitHubEnvs fails on the orgs-without-token guard, and TestFailureIfGitBackupDirUndefined fails because GIT_BACKUP_DIR is unset. Every other Run-driving test skips without a token or SOBA_LIVE_GITHUB_TESTS. TestGithubRepositoryBackupWithMockAPI calls githosts directly. The table is new code in this change. The current pairings (Gitea, GitHub, Gitlab, AzureDevOps, Sourcehut) are correct, so nothing is wrong for users. A test someone could add is not a promised outcome, so this is an improvement. The reviewer's mutation run could not be reproduced because execution is unavailable.

items.consequence: The directory that startup creates and the directory each backup run uses and then deletes are computed by two separate copies of the same rule (GIT_WORKING_DIR if set, else <backupDir>/.working). If one copy is later changed (for example to honour a _FILE variant or to trim the value) startup will create one directory while runs clone into and clean up another. The refactor lifted the startup copy out of Run into its own helper, createWorkingDir, but left the inline rule instead of calling resolveWorkingDir, which sits 330 lines above and is already used by runProviderBackups; calling it makes the two paths agree by construction and removes four lines with no behaviour change.
items.proposedFix: In createWorkingDir (internal/backup.go:473-478) replace the comment, the os.Getenv(envGitWorkingDir) read and the empty-string fallback with `workingDIR := resolveWorkingDir(backupDIR)`. resolveWorkingDir (internal/backup.go:140-146) returns exactly the same value for every input, so the log line and MkdirAll call that follow are unaffected.
items.notes: Every original item, known problem and corrective request was assessed.

claims.notes: The comment says the new createWorkingDir helper repeats the GIT_WORKING_DIR-or-<backupDir>/.working rule instead of calling resolveWorkingDir, so the two could drift apart. True: createWorkingDir reads os.Getenv(envGitWorkingDir) and falls back to filepath.Join(backupDIR, workingDIRName), and resolveWorkingDir computes the same value. createWorkingDir is a helper this change adds. Today both give identical results, so nothing fails and the divergence is only possible in the future. Nothing is promised to fail, so this is an improvement.

items.claim: New shared backupStatusTitle helper has no test
items.consequence: An operator could be told "soba backups succeeded" for a run where every provider failed, on ntfy, Slack and Telegram at once, without any test failing. The PR folds three copies of the status switch into one helper, so a mistake there now affects every notifier, yet nothing asserts which title each (succeeded, failed) pair yields; no test references backupStatusTitle, sendNtfy, sendSlackMessage or sendTelegramMessage. Swapping the succeeded and failed titles on a scratch copy of the reviewed commit left all credential-free tests passing. The helper is pure, so a four-row table test closes the gap.
items.proposedFix: Add TestBackupStatusTitle (e.g. in internal/util_test.go, next to TestGetBackupsStatsAdditional) asserting backupStatusTitle(2,0) == titleBackupsSucceeded, backupStatusTitle(1,1) == titleBackupsErrors, backupStatusTitle(0,3) == titleBackupsFailed and backupStatusTitle(0,0) == titleBackupsFailed. Additionally assert the three constants against their literal strings (including the leading U+FE0F on the errors and failed titles) so the user-visible text the PR promises to keep is pinned rather than compared to itself.
items.notes: Every original item, known problem and corrective request was assessed.

claims.quote: New shared backupStatusTitle helper has no test
claims.notes: The comment says nothing tests the new backupStatusTitle helper that every notifier now shares, so a swapped title would pass the suite. True: none of the test files reads backupStatusTitle, sendNtfy, sendSlackMessage, sendTelegramMessage or the title constants. webhook_test.go covers only sendWebhook. The helper and its constants are added by this change. The current mapping is correct (succeeded>0 and failed==0 gives succeeded; both >0 gives errors; otherwise failed). This is a test someone could add, not a lost protection, so it is an improvement.
